item.title: Inside MITA's war room where cyberattacks are detected and repelled
item.description: A feature published on Wednesday examines how the Malta Information Technology Agency guards the state's IT infrastructure from its headquarters in Santa Venera, as artificial intelligence reshapes cyberwarfare. The report focuses on the risks posed by rapidly evolving technology to government workers handling sensitive data, and on MITA's detection, anticipation and repelling of cyberattacks.

item.title: Three Malta consortia bid for the €1.8 billion St Vincent de Paul hospital tender
item.description: Three Malta-based joint ventures submitted bids on Wednesday for one of the largest tenders in Maltese history, covering the build, operation and running of the new hospital at St Vincent de Paul. The government had estimated the contract at around €1.38 billion, but all three bids came in hundreds of millions of euros higher. CareLink Medical Group, involving the Saint James hospital group and Corinthia group shareholders, bid €1.74 billion; Custodia Care, led by Vassallo Group's CareMalta with care home firm CareRise, bid €1.79 billion; and Proxima, led by a firm owned by James Caterers, submitted the highest bid at €1.87 billion. The award is not yet decided.

item.title: Murder accused Lorin Scicluna taken to scene of Lassana Cisse killing, breaks down in tears
item.description: Seven years after Lassana Cisse was shot dead on a road in Birżebbuġa, the man accused of his murder visited the scene on Wednesday, accompanied by the judge and jurors hearing his trial. The 29-year-old former soldier broke down in tears during the visit, Newsbook reported. Cisse, a 42-year-old father of two from the Ivory Coast, was killed on April 6, 2019 while walking home after watching football with friends; he was shot three times and died on the spot. Scicluna, arrested in May 2019 while accompanying an Armed Forces of Malta marching band in Naxxar, is also charged with the attempted murder of two other men and a hit-and-run; all four victims are Black.

item.title: Cutajar 'not personally comfortable' with Budget 2027 measures on TCNs
item.description: Equality Minister Rosianne Cutajar said she is not personally comfortable with the Budget 2027 measures affecting third-country nationals, though she understands the difficult decision the finance minister had to make. Under the measures, TCNs without long-term residency lose free childcare and public transport and face higher work-permit renewal fees. Cutajar said she had raised her concerns with Finance Minister Clyde Caruana and warned the measures risk fuelling anti-foreigner sentiment and a deeper division between people.

item.title: Total tax revenue reached almost €7.5 billion in 2025, NSO says
item.description: Total tax revenue stood at €7,471.6 million in 2025, an increase of €698.9 million over the previous year, the National Statistics Office said. The figure equalled a tax burden of 30.3 per cent, up from 29.3 per cent of GDP in 2024, and accounted for 86.4 per cent of total general government revenue. Direct taxes contributed €3,757.0 million and VAT rose to €1.64 billion, with households accounting for 54 per cent of income tax collected.

item.title: Over 1,000 sign petition urging Malta to scrap new TCN work permit fees
item.description: A Change.org petition calling on government to scrap the planned increases in work permit fees and a new annual contribution for third-country nationals had gathered 1,056 verified signatures by Wednesday. The petition was launched by a foreign worker who says they have lived and worked legally in Malta since 2022, paying taxes and social security throughout. The author warns the extra costs would hit workers earning between €1,200 and €1,600 a month particularly hard, especially those already struggling with rising rents and utility bills.

item.title: Missing 13-year-old girl last seen in Tarxien has been found
item.description: Police appealed for help on Wednesday to locate 13-year-old Shanyrielle Formosa, who had been reported missing and was last seen in the Tarxien area, before updating the appeal to confirm she had been found. The initial police statement invited anyone with information to contact the police on 2122 4001 or 119, or to visit the nearest police station. Newsbook reported the girl had been located earlier on Wednesday.

item.title: Court urges authorities to help foreign worker despite rejecting permit appeal
item.description: A court has urged immigration authorities to give a foreign worker another chance to obtain a residence and work permit, despite dismissing his appeal as filed too late. The case follows Dan Bahadur Khamcha's single permit application, which Identità refused because his immigration status was irregular when submitted, after his employer Royal Brothers Group failed to renew its licence. The Immigration Appeals Board declared the appeal null and void in October 2025, and he appealed to the Court of Appeal in February 2026.

item.title: 'I'm living from pay to pay': TCNs worried about budget measures
item.description: Third-country nationals interviewed by Times of Malta described mounting financial anxiety over the new budget measures. American Kyle Thomas, in Malta for six years and working in sales in Ħal Far, said he was already living from paycheque to paycheque and relies on buses to get to work each day. A Moroccan man who studied in Malta and holds a master's degree said he may have to give up his car and is considering leaving the island, while an Indian mother said she and her husband may not be able to save for a better future for their daughter.

item.title: Project Green's urban greening budget gets a €20 million trim
item.description: Project Green's budget for urban greening has been cut by a third, from €30 million this year to €20 million in 2027, after years of underspending on flagship projects. Urban greening was a government priority ahead of the 2022 general election, when Robert Abela pledged €700 million to create urban 'green lungs'. The agency says it has completed 36 open spaces with 25 further projects underway, and an environment ministry spokesperson said urban greening remains a priority beyond Project Green's specific remit.

item.title: Momentum calls for national plan to strengthen dementia care
item.description: Momentum has called for a clear national plan to strengthen dementia care in Malta, following the death of Charles Zammit, a serving police sergeant who retired after 35 years and died after a long hospital stay awaiting a secure specialist ward. Dementia experts Dr Anthony Scerri and Professor Charles Scerri estimated around 8,000 people were living with dementia in Malta in 2021, a figure expected to rise to more than 21,500 by 2060. The party argues general hospital wards are not designed to provide long-term care in a specialised, safe residential environment.

item.title: Women's Lobby welcomes Budget measures but flags childcare and parental leave gaps
item.description: The Malta Women's Lobby welcomed Budget 2027 measures that it said will make a difference to women's lives, but expressed disappointment over the omission of parental leave reforms, free childcare for some third-country nationals, and therapy for children experiencing trauma. The lobby noted Labour's electoral manifesto had pledged to extend maternity and paternity leave and introduce six months of state-paid parental leave, none of which featured in the Budget speech. It said care-related challenges cannot be addressed through tax incentives alone.

item.title: Organisations express anger over Montekristo Park permit to reopen
item.description: Several organisations expressed disgust and anger on Wednesday over the decision to grant Montekristo Park a permit to reopen to the public, and called for more transparency on how the decision was taken. In a joint statement, the organisations said the case raises questions about accountability, equality before the law and the exercise of political power in Malta. They noted the operator already has a conviction for breaching animal welfare laws and asked for the permit, its legal basis and assessment details to be published.

item.title: Malta undecided on participation in new EU Lebanon mission
item.description: Malta supports a newly agreed EU civilian and military mission in Lebanon, but any decision on participation will depend on further assessment, the Foreign Affairs Ministry said. EU foreign ministers decided on 11 October to set up the EU Support Mission in Lebanon, which has an initial mandate of three years to strengthen the country's security forces. A ministry spokesperson said further discussions within the EU Foreign Affairs Council and operational planning are required before the mission can be deployed.

item.title: Son accused of threatening parents for drug money found hiding on boat
item.description: A 24-year-old man from Żabbar was remanded in custody on Wednesday after pleading not guilty to threatening and intimidating his parents for money to sustain his drug addiction, before allegedly fleeing the family home and hiding on a boat for two days. He was arraigned under arrest facing charges including domestic violence, harassment, causing fear of violence, breaching bail conditions and recidivism. The prosecution said the situation escalated on Monday, 26 October.

item.title: Over 5,300 patients to get two mental health medications for free
item.description: More than 5,300 patients are expected to benefit from two mental health medications being made available free of charge through the government's Pharmacy of Your Choice scheme. The Health Ministry said Escitalopram and Alprazolam will be added to the Government Formulary, with an annual investment of approximately €355,000. The initiative forms part of Malta's National Mental Health Strategy, and treatment can be initiated by consultants in psychiatry, neurology and geriatrics as well as family doctors.

item.title: Murder accused Lorin Scicluna takes the stand in the Lassana Cisse trial
item.description: Lorin Scicluna took the witness stand on Wednesday in his trial for the 2019 murder of Lassana Cisse, telling jurors his account of the night the Ivory Coast father of two was shot dead in Birżebbuġa. Earlier in the day he accompanied the judge and jurors to the crime scene, where he broke down in tears. The prosecution closed its case and the defence confirmed the accused would testify; Scicluna admitted fabricating his initial statement to police because he feared revealing what Francesco Fenech had done, and described how he and friends drove to Ħal Far to provoke migrants.

item.title: Abela defends Budget 2027 TCN measures: 'Which country gives all services for free?'
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela defended the Budget 2027 measures affecting third-country nationals, asking which country gives all services free to everyone who arrives. He said foreign workers are paid according to sector and insisted government remains committed to treating them with dignity, while arguing that the State cannot provide every service free of charge. Central Bank figures tabled in parliament by Finance Minister Clyde Caruana show median TCN employment income 38 per cent below the national average.

item.title: 24 organisations brand Budget 2027 TCN measures 'socially unjust'
item.description: A coalition of 24 social and cultural organisations said Budget 2027 measures affecting third-country nationals are socially unjust and anti-worker. The joint statement argued that foreign workers are already among the most vulnerable to poverty, social exclusion and workplace abuse, and questioned whether removing free transport and childcare while raising permit and transport costs is compatible with constitutional and EU non-discrimination rules. The groups are calling on government to reverse the measures and place workers' rights and dignity ahead of profit.

item.title: Turkish firm GiMAS opens €10 million wind turbine factory in Ħal Far
item.description: Turkish industrial company GiMAS opened a €10 million factory in Ħal Far making parts for wind turbines, employing over 40 people in its first years. It is the company's first manufacturing plant outside Turkey and gives it a base inside the EU market. Prime Minister Robert Abela said the small workforce was a strength because the project adds high-value work without extra pressure on infrastructure, and linked it to national strategies on renewable energy running to 2035 and 2050, including possible offshore wind farms.

item.title: National equality body calls for impact assessment on new foreign worker policies
item.description: The National Commission for the Promotion of Equality has called on government to carry out an Equality Impact Assessment before measures targeting third-country nationals come into force. The NCPE warned several proposals could deepen inequalities among vulnerable groups, with women and minority ethnic members of staff likely to be disproportionately affected where low incomes and insecure work intersect with other discrimination factors. It said TCNs are among the lowest-paid workers in Malta and that burdens placed on them rather than on those benefiting from their labour would hit the most vulnerable hardest.

item.title: APS Bank profit jumps to record €35m in first nine months of 2026
item.description: APS Bank reported a record pre-tax profit of €34.5 million at group level for the nine months to 30 September 2026, up 94 per cent from €17.8 million in the same period last year. At bank level pre-tax profit reached €35.4 million. Net interest income grew 37.5 per cent to €77.7 million on expanding retail and commercial lending and stronger treasury yields, while interest expense fell to €25.6 million from €34.7 million, lifting the net interest margin to 2.23 per cent from 1.80 per cent.

item.title: PN questions how Budget 2027 will address infrastructural pressures
item.description: Opposition MPs Alex Perici Calascione and Rebekah Borg said the government's budget measures fail to detail how funds will be channelled towards infrastructural pressures created by Malta's economic model. They argued Finance Minister Clyde Caruana did not explain how revenue would be spent upgrading infrastructure, and said attracting quality tourists requires surrounding areas and hotspots to match accommodation. Both said operators had contacted the opposition over the announced rise in eco-contribution on tourist accommodation.

item.title: Childcare groups warn Budget 2027 TCN measures will cost the economy
item.description: The Malta Women's Lobby warned that making childcare unaffordable pushes mothers out of work and into informal, unprotected jobs, while the Malta Chamber of SMEs and childcare centre providers said removing free childcare for TCNs without long-term residency was decided without consultation. The lobby said the omission of parental leave reforms and therapy for children experiencing trauma were gaps in the budget. The Chamber said around 25 per cent of children in childcare come from third countries and that operators had already planned for the change from February 2027.

item.title: 'Mqabba murder flags cycle of intergenerational abuse': violence commissioner
item.description: Commissioner for Gender-Based Violence and Domestic Violence Samantha Pace Gasan said the murder of a woman by her son in Mqabba is a clear example of intergenerational abuse. Referring to the case of Mary Grace Cassar, she said the culture of abuse permeates generations, with victims and perpetrators often having themselves been victims of abuse. She stressed the case is still before the court and the charges remain allegations, and called for education, victim support, perpetrator programmes and anonymous reporting to break the cycle.

item.title: Man stole restaurant umbrellas to pay for wife's medication, court told
item.description: A 62-year-old man from Żabbar admitted stealing five sunshades worth about €2,500 from two restaurants in Marsaxlokk over three nights in October, to afford medication for his sick wife. Charles Spiteri was granted bail pending sentencing, with a €5,000 personal guarantee, a nightly curfew, a ban from Marsaxlokk and no contact with witnesses. The prosecution agreed with the defence that he stole the umbrellas to buy his wife's medication, and the court was told he also struggles with drug addiction. Judgment is due on 5 November.

item.title: New cheque rules come into force on 1 January 2027
item.description: New rules on cheques in Malta will take effect on 1 January 2027, following a Bank of Malta directive on drafts and cheques. Three main changes apply: cheques may only be issued for €50 or more, no cheque may be cashed directly and must instead be deposited into the payee's bank account, and cheques remain valid for three months from issue. Anyone receiving a cheque will therefore have to deposit it within three months rather than cash it at the counter.

item.title: Ryanair moves airport bag-drop cut-off to 60 minutes from 10 November
item.description: Ryanair has said passengers with checked bags must now be at the airport bag drop 60 minutes before their scheduled flight time, rather than 40, from 10 November. The airline said the earlier cut-off gives passengers more time to clear security and passport control and reach the gate, particularly in busy periods. Around 20 per cent of the airline's passengers use the bag drop service and will be affected, while the 80 per cent who check in online and travel with hand luggage only are not impacted.

item.title: 222 children adopted by Maltese parents between 2015 and 2026
item.description: A total of 222 children were adopted by Maltese parents between 2015 and 2026, according to information tabled in Parliament. The largest number came from India, with 168 children adopted between 2016 and 2026, while a further 29 came from Portugal and Slovakia, Russia and Bulgaria each accounted for seven. The Ministry for Social Policy and the Family noted that figures covering the years before 2022 may contain statistical discrepancies due to limited information available at the time.

item.title: Employers often unsure how to deal with workplace harassment, conference hears
item.description: Panelists at a Malta Chamber conference on gender-based violence as a business issue said employers generally do not look away from harassment cases but often do not know what to do next. Examples included inappropriate compliments and an HR manager accused of abuse after trying to protect a tipsy employee at a staff party. Malta Chamber's Ramona Galea and HR consultant Mariella Galea said more awareness is needed to help employers identify cases and respond, as HR professionals can become overwhelmed.

item.title: Man jailed 14 months for drug possession
item.description: A man was sentenced to 14 months in prison and fined €800 after pleading guilty to five drug-related offences. Alejandro Monrosy Lopez, a Colombian national, was charged with possession of cocaine, MDMA, ecstasy, ketamine and pink cocaine in circumstances indicating the drugs were not intended exclusively for personal use. The court took his early guilty plea, cooperation with the police and clean record into account, and ordered the seized money and drugs to be confiscated.

item.title: Malta among 36 countries confirmed for Eurovision 2027
item.description: Thirty-six countries have confirmed they will take part in the Eurovision Song Contest 2027, to be held in Burgas, Bulgaria, with Malta among them. The semi-finals and final will take place on 11, 13 and 15 May at the Arena Burgas. Canada will compete for the first time while North Macedonia returns after four years, and Spain and Slovenia have until December to confirm. Thirty-one songs will be split across the two semi-finals, with ten from each advancing to the final.
